observations: A large yellow disc fills the upper two-thirds, ringed by concentric yellow lines and covered with black zigzag marks, dot clusters, and a curved line forming a simple smiling mouth.
Two diagonal black bars cross the disc, each tipped with white triangular teeth; white streaks descend from the eye-dot area toward the lower half.
The background is deep red with layered blue-grey brushwork at the top; three yellow cross-hatched diamond shapes float in the lower field, and red scratch marks cut across the whole surface.
reading: A yellow disc carries a grinning face, but the smile sits below crossed bars edged with teeth, and white streaks run down from its eye dots. The heavy red field below presses against the disc's brightness. The zigzag border and scattered marks give the face a restless surface, while the floating yellow diamonds below read as echoes or debris. The mood sits somewhere between celebration and unease.
contextAngle: Within the owned nnotb subset, this work sits between title neighbors nnxyz nnotb #261 and nnxyz nnotb #263. The dense layering and red-dominant field contrast sharply with #263's spare two-color silhouette, showing the range the collector values across this owned group.

connections.reason: Both works place face-like forms with visible teeth at center, but #261 uses looping white outlines on blue while #262 builds its face from a solid yellow disc on red, making the shared tooth motif land very differently.

Both pair a saturated red ground with a yellow focal mass and use circular or looping marks within that mass, though rawblocks #28 places its yellow form at the top edge while #262 centers its disc as the dominant shape.

lookingQuestion: The white streaks descend from the eye-dot area of the disc — do they read as part of the face's structure, or as something separate breaking through it?
ambiguities: A small red-and-blue elongated shape near the top of the disc is unclear — it may be a secondary object or a mark within the disc's surface.
The title content 'nnotb' is treated as a collection identifier only; no meaning is inferred from it.
